claims.statement: The EEG-BIDS paper identifies diverse EEG formats as an impediment to reuse and large-scale databases and states that structured BIDS data enable automated, reproducible analysis workflows.
The EEG-BIDS ecosystem already includes a free validator and converters in MNE-Python, EEGLAB and FieldTrip, proving interoperability while also creating strong open-source competition.

Recent published EEG datasets continue to use custom conversion scripts to move native acquisition formats into BIDS-compatible EDF and metadata structures, indicating continuing practical integration work.

contrary_evidence: BIDS Validator, MNE-BIDS, EEGLAB, FieldTrip and ezBIDS already provide substantial free conversion and validation capability.
Academic labs often have low budgets and may assign curation to students rather than buy software.
The available evidence establishes workflow friction but not commercial willingness to pay.

economics.acquisition_route: Complete three paid archival-data conversions with fixed acceptance criteria, recruit one EEG distributor or core facility, then package the repeated mappings and QC report as a licence.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Three hundred lab licences averaging 15000 PLN annually plus one hundred assisted projects averaging 25000 PLN would produce 7m PLN annual revenue. At a mature blended 38% owner-cash margin, about 2.66m PLN per year could yield more than 10m PLN cumulative distributions over five mature years without sale proceeds.
economics.founder_time: Use public or customer-authorised datasets and support only two device families at 3-4 hours/day, clearly limiting the product to research data management; remain employed until annual renewals and contribution margin meet the stated gates.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Local software licences can exceed 85% gross margin; assisted curation is expert labour, yielding a blended target of 60-75% until mapping and QC are automated.
economics.payback: Target buyer payback within one dataset by replacing several days of senior analyst curation and reducing handoff rework; the current labour baseline must be measured lab by lab.
economics.pricing: Assumption to test: 12000-30000 PLN annual lab licence, 8000-40000 PLN per assisted dataset depending on subjects and formats, and a higher private-deployment tier for CROs.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Labs acquire new subjects and studies continuously, and stable manifests become part of their analysis pipeline; grant cycles and open-source alternatives can create episodic demand.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing device-format and metadata-mapping library plus anonymised QC distributions and adjudicated artifact patterns reduces setup time across labs while raw human data remain local.
fingerprint.customer: University EEG core facilities, small neuroscience CROs and preclinical or research-only neurotech teams handling repeated multi-subject datasets across device formats.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: EEG equipment distributors, university core facilities, research-software consultants and grant-data-management partners refer projects; documentation and reproducible example datasets support self-serve global adoption.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Desktop/container workflow that maps vendor files to EEG-BIDS, validates required metadata, runs configurable signal-quality checks, creates review queues and signs a reproducible manifest of raw-to-curated transformations; annual licence plus assisted dataset packages.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A lab manager, PI, CRO project lead or neurotech R&D head pays per dataset and for an annual team workspace; existing spend is analyst or research-assistant curation time and licensed acquisition/analysis software.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A recording batch must be handed from acquisition staff to analysts, shared across sites, archived for a grant or prepared for publication, but naming, events, channel metadata and artifact decisions are inconsistent.

founder_fit: EEG and neuroscience are direct founder interests, while signal QC and reproducible pipelines use existing data-science strengths.
A local-first product reduces regulated-data hosting burden and can be sold globally from Warsaw.
Self-serve technical content and equipment/core-facility channels fit a low-public-persona preference.
Service-assisted curation can validate paid demand before a large software build, within the first 100000 PLN.
risks: Research users may mistakenly treat QC output as clinical interpretation unless scope is explicit.
Human-subject files can contain sensitive or re-identifiable data even when processed locally.
Format and metadata edge cases can turn a software product into bespoke consulting.
Open-source improvements could eliminate the conversion wedge before a paid distribution channel forms.

structure.commercial_archetype: Research-workflow software with per-dataset assisted curation
structure.control_point: The signed raw-to-BIDS manifest accepted before analysis, collaboration or publication
structure.critical_dependency: Labs must value support and auditability beyond open-source converters, and local execution must accommodate their device formats and ethics constraints

thesis: Build a local-first workspace for EU EEG research labs, CROs and neurotech teams that converts heterogeneous recordings to EEG-BIDS, checks metadata and signal quality, records human artifact decisions and emits a reproducible dataset manifest. Buyers already spend researcher, technician and bioinformatician time preparing datasets for analysis, collaboration and publication; the commercial wedge is a validated, service-assisted handoff rather than another analysis algorithm.
title: Local-First EEG Dataset Curation and Quality-Control Workspace
uncertainties: The number of European labs with repeated paid curation demand and budgets outside grants is unknown.
It is unclear whether signal QC should remain generic or require study-specific methods too costly to productise.
CRO procurement, device-distributor incentives and acceptable local deployment models need interviews and paid trials.
All pricing, margins, customer volumes and wealth projections are assumptions.
